title: What If You Walked Far Fewer Than 10,000 Steps a Day?

scenes.text: What if 10,000 steps was never a science number? It started as a product name.
In 1965, a Japanese company sold a pedometer called Manpo-kei, which means ten thousand step meter.
An epidemiologist calls it a made up number. No study had tested ten thousand steps at the time.
In a study of 16,741 older women, those averaging 4,400 steps had 41 percent lower mortality than those near 2,700.
The benefit leveled off around 7,500 steps a day.
A 2025 Lancet analysis found about 7,000 steps was linked to nearly 50 percent lower mortality than about 2,000.

description:
What if 10,000 steps was never a science number?
It began as a 1965 pedometer name, and research shows benefits well below it.
